column2: `persist_handoff` must write `.step-8-ship-handoff.rc` (and json) before removing `.bg-wait-active`. if marker removal precedes the rc write, a `<task-notification>` in that window can see no live marker and no rc yet, misclassifying terminal notifications as premature and blocking `route-exit`, or leaving hooks in an inconsistent state during the real completion window.

the plan resets no-progress state on entry but does not clear `bg-poll-guard-probe-denials.step-8-ship-handoff.rc.count` before arming the new marker. fresh step 8 reruns in the same `implement_tmpdir` (stall recovery, ci-fix loops) can inherit a stale absent-rc count and deny the first legal `test -f "$implement_tmpdir/.step-8-ship-handoff.rc"` probe before the new wait observes its own state, breaking never #8 recovery and acceptance criterion 4.

step 8 rc probe clamp needs its own sentinel-basename extractor. `probe_sentinel_name` only parses `.completed/(step-3-terminal|step-5c-terminal|step-final-summary)` paths, so a `test -f "$implement_tmpdir/.step-8-ship-handoff.rc"` probe will not resolve a counter key, the clamp helper will fail-open (`|| exit 0`), and repeated absent-rc probes stay unlimited, defeating the storm cap and planned threshold test.

step 8 rc-probe allowance still assumes a singleton live dir or only binds explicit `design_tmpdir` probes. if any other session has an active bg-wait marker, the sanctioned `test -f "$implement_tmpdir/.step-8-ship-handoff.rc"` recovery probe can be denied or mis-attributed even though the step 8 marker is live, breaking the multiple-live-waits edge case in feature scope.

if writing `.step-8-ship-handoff.rc` or `.step-8-ship-handoff.json` trips `set -e`, the exit trap can exit before removing `.bg-wait-active`, leaving notification-storm hooks armed after the ship wrapper has exited.

the plan registers `.step-8-ship-handoff.rc` as the hook release sentinel but does not extend `bash_attempts_terminal_sentinel_mutation`, which today only matches `.completed/*-terminal` paths. a `touch`, `: >`, `printf >`, or similar write to the rc file is not a probe verb and bypasses the step 8 rc-probe classifier, so forged regular files can be treated as completion while `ship pr` is still running. planned hook tests also omit this mutation-deny coverage, so the gap can land undetected.

the planned skill edit adds hook-allowed/clamped language for the rc probe but does not update the existing never #8 sentence listing hook-covered `/implement` markers as only `implement-step3-checks` and `implement-step5-review`. operators and structure readers still see ship-pr as probe-only, not marker-backed, conflicting with acceptance criteria and the new `step=implement-step8-ship` contract.

the planned test updates never force a non-zero `python/cli.py ship pr` exit after `.bg-wait-active` is armed. a regression in the normal long-running driver failure path could leave the marker behind or preserve stale handoff sidecars, and the current test matrix would still pass.

reship/ci-fix relaunch leaves prior handoff sidecars visible to the rc probe until the new wrapper clears them. the plan clears stale `.step-8-ship-handoff.rc`/`.json` only inside `step-8-ship.sh` entry. on `next_action=reship` or ci-fix re-entry, the orchestrator can launch another immediate-background `step-8-ship.sh` while the previous run's rc/json still exist. a spurious early `<task-notification>` in the startup window can satisfy `test -f "$implement_tmpdir/.step-8-ship-handoff.rc"` and re-enter `route-exit` with stale json before the new wrapper deletes those files.

`step8_handoff_probe_clamp` must detect rc presence at `$dir/.step-8-ship-handoff.rc`, not under `.completed/`. the plan says to mirror `terminal_sentinel_probe_clamp`, which treats presence as `$dir/.completed/$name`. step 8 release sentinel is `$dir/.step-8-ship-handoff.rc` at tmpdir root. a copied check never sees rc present, so the clamp counter never clears on completion, repeated absent-rc probes hit the threshold, and the sanctioned never #8 recovery probe is denied while ship-pr is still running.

the planned never #8 edit adds implement-step8-ship inventory and hook-allowed/clamped language but does not require revising the existing sentence that foreground terminal-sentinel probing is design-only and "/implement recovery is notification-only." that line sits in the same never rule as the step 8 `test -f .step-8-ship-handoff.rc` carve-out. operators can read notification-only as banning the one sanctioned implement probe and skip it on premature notifications, leaving storms uncapped.

putting `rm -f` for `.step-8-ship-handoff.rc`/`.json` inside the same bash fence as `step-8-ship.sh` is wrong on two axes. that fence runs under `run_in_background: true`, so a spurious `<task-notification>` can still route to stale handoff files before the child’s first `rm`. post–step-0 fence-shape rules also require a single launcher line (`bash "$implement_tmpdir/larch-run.sh" …`) and reject `;`, `&&`, `||`, and multi-command fences, so an inline `rm` in the launcher block fails `test-implement-fence-shape.sh` / `make lint` unless the plan adds a separate allowed fence (or an approved one-line launcher target).

the plan revises never #8 from blanket `/implement` notification-only recovery (and the `/design`-only foreground-probe carve-out sentence) to scoped steps 3/5 vs step 8 language, but does not update `scripts/test-implement-anti-polling-rule.sh`, which still pins the old literals in `skills/implement/skill.md`, `skills/shared/orchestrator-never.md`, and `agents.md`. landing skill edits alone leaves `make test-implement-anti-polling-rule` / `make test-harnesses-5` / `make lint` red and preserves operator-facing contradictions with the sanctioned step 8 `test -f .step-8-ship-handoff.rc` path.

the plan names `stall-recovery step8-shippr`, ci-fix, and conflict-resolution phase 4 as paths that need orchestrator pre-launch clear, but only `skills/implement/skill.md` is slated for fence edits. load-on-demand references (`stall-recovery.md`, ship-pr ci-fix, conflict-resolution phase 4) tell the orchestrator to re-invoke `step-8-ship.sh` with the immediate-background contract and no stale-handoff step, so a `step8-shippr` reship can still hit the startup-window race before wrapper-entry cleanup runs.

skills/implement/skill.md:654-657 [scope-reduction] orchestrator stale-handoff `rm` in the step 8 launch fence conflicts with `test-implement-fence-shape.sh` one-line new-shape rule. scenario: the plan requires `rm -f "$implement_tmpdir/.step-8-ship-handoff.rc" "$implement_tmpdir/.step-8-ship-handoff.json"` inside the same ````bash` fence as `bash "$implement_tmpdir/larch-run.sh" skills/implement/scripts/step-8-ship.sh`. `scripts/test-implement-fence-shape.sh` `validate_new` rejects any new-shape fence with more than one nonblank physical line and also rejects `;` / `&&` compound commands. `make test-implement-fence-shape` / `make lint` fails even if hook and wrapper work.

the plan revises `skills/shared/orchestrator-never.md` to scoped steps 3/5 vs step 8 recovery and updates `scripts/test-implement-anti-polling-rule.sh`, but `scripts/test-design-structure.sh` line 192 still requires the old blanket literal `for `/implement`, when a premature <task-notification> fires while the child is still running (empty or non-empty task output), end the turn without sentinel probing` via a `contains` pin on `orchestrator-never.md`. that harness runs under `make test-design-structure` / `make test-harnesses-3`. landing orchestrator-never edits without updating this pin leaves ci red even when runtime hooks and the anti-polling harness pass.

branch re-entry references still tell operators to re-invoke `step-8-ship.sh` without a foreground stale-handoff clear. affected paths: `skills/implement/references/stall-recovery.md` (lines 44–45), `skills/implement/references/ship-pr-ci-fix.md` (line 23), `skills/implement/references/conflict-resolution.md` (lines 5, 7, 15), and `skills/implement/references/ship-pr-exit-matrix.md` (lines 39, 41, 56–58). these are the actual rerun surfaces for reship, ci-fix, and conflict-resolution. leaving them unchanged preserves the startup-window stale `.step-8-ship-handoff.{rc,json}` race on the branches this feature is meant to harden.
